details:
Q1: Which plan/implement runs should move behind the new privilege boundary? That means an isolated container with no access to `GH_PAT`, the credentialed checkout or the Docker socket, killed when its step ends, with authenticated collection and Git publication kept on the trusted host side.
Choices:
A) Only runs for workflow-heal issues (`ai:workflow-heal` / heal-evidence issues), for both plan and implement. Ordinary issues keep today's host editor path unchanged. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Every plan and implement editor run, heal or not. This removes the host-editor credential exposure everywhere but is a much larger, higher-risk change.
C) Implement only for heal issues. Plan keeps the host path and receives the bounded diagnostics as plain prompt text.
Q2: What trusted source fixes the enforced file allowlist for a heal issue? It must be set before untrusted evidence is processed, so neither the evidence nor the plan can widen it.
Choices:
A) The intake writes a versioned scope marker into the heal issue at creation (for example `<!-- ai:workflow-heal-scope:v1 -->`). It lists paths taken only from deterministic, validated report fields: `crash_file`, the failing workflow file, and ownership-classified `changed_files` that exist at the support ref. It also always adds `tests/**` and `changelog.d/*.md` for the required regression test and changelog fragment. Implement accepts the marker only when the issue's author is the `GH_PAT` account and the body was not edited after creation. (RECOMMENDED)
B) A fixed directory allowlist for every heal issue (`scripts/`, `prompts/`, `.github/workflows/`, `.github/actions/`, `tests/`, `changelog.d/`), independent of the report.
C) Option A's per-report marker without the automatic `tests/**` / `changelog.d/` additions. Strictest, but a deterministic-failure heal could not add its required regression test.
Q3: When a heal issue has no valid trusted scope (missing, edited or untrusted marker), how should implement fail closed?
Choices:
A) Refuse the run and label the issue `ai:needs-human` with a comment naming the reason. This avoids `ai:scope-blocked`, whose label event itself triggers `workflow_failure_heal.yml` and could start another heal for the same issue. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Refuse and label `ai:scope-blocked`, accepting that this re-enters the heal reporter (the lineage cap still bounds it).
C) Refuse with a comment and `ai:implementation-failed` only, leaving recovery to the stall poller.
